elements.evidence: Section 15.16 as redlined still binds both Parties: "neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder..." Customer therefore remains subject to a non-solicitation restriction; the preferred position (deletion of any restriction on Customer) is not taken.
"neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party" — the obligation runs symmetrically against both Customer and Vendor; the carve-outs likewise refer to "the Parties' right" and "a Party".

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder" — i.e., personnel directly involved in the contracted development/services work, not all personnel.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Redline replaces "During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter" with "For twelve (12) months after an employee's involvement in the development activities hereunder ends" — the temporal anchor is now the end of the individual's involvement and the period is exactly twelve months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained sentence: "nothing herein shall restrict or preclude the Parties' right to make generalized searches for employees by way of a general solicitation for employment placed in a trade journal, newspaper or website".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Added to the same carve-out sentence: "or to respond to any employee who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis" — an express unsolicited-approach exclusion operating on the same "nothing herein shall restrict or preclude" stem.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is solicitation-only — "shall not solicit ... to terminate his or her employment and accept employment or work as a consultant with the soliciting Party". No "employ or engage" / "no-hire" language appears anywhere in the rendered clause.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative language: mutuality, involved-personnel scope, twelve months from the end of involvement, general-advertising carve-out, unsolicited-approach carve-out, and solicitation-only (no no-hire) are each satisfied in the rendered text rather than merely promised in the comment.
Preferred is not met and is not claimed: the clause still binds Customer, so the finding correctly targets the fallback level rather than deleting Section 15.16.

Original clause was a genuine fallback failure on two material terms — an undisclosed ([***]) tail running from expiry of the Term rather than from the end of the individual's involvement, and no unsolicited-approach carve-out — so 'deviation' is the correct status; the general-advertising carve-out and involved-personnel scope were already compliant and were correctly left untouched.

Minimality holds: exactly two surgical edits (temporal anchor and one appended carve-out phrase). No survival tail, expense language, procedure, damages category, or other model-language extra was added; the retained mutual scope, the solicitation-only formulation and the existing carve-out wording are preserved verbatim, and the only deleted words ('During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter') are the duration element itself.

Intent is preserved: removing the Term-based anchor leaves no dangling cross-reference (the defined term 'Term' remains in use elsewhere and Section 15.16 no longer depends on it), the new twelve-month clock is self-executing off an ascertainable event, and no retained sentence contradicts the added unsolicited-approach exclusion since it hangs off the same 'Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall restrict or preclude' stem.

Deterministic checks were inspected in substance, not just mechanically: both operations in fact land in the rendered text, the duration match is a true twelve-month cap measured from the end of involvement (not a request- or expiry-based deadline), and the carve-out gate corresponds to actual carve-out language.
